title: Are we ready to measure running power? Repeatability and concurrent validity of five commercial technologies
authors: Cerezuela-Espejo V, Hernandez-Belmonte A, Courel-Ibanez J, Conesa-Ros E, Mora-Rodriguez R, Pallares JG
population: 12 endurance-trained male athletes; test-retest on a treadmill and an athletic track, three submaximal protocols varying speed, body weight and slope
findings: Five technologies (Stryd app, Stryd watch, RunScribe, Garmin running power, Polar Vantage) were compared with VO2 from a metabolic cart.
Stryd was the most repeatable in all environments and conditions (SEM <= 12.5 W, CV <= 4.3%, ICC >= 0.980) and had the best concurrent validity with VO2 (r >= 0.911, SEE <= 7.3%).
Polar, Garmin and RunScribe power kept some relationship with VO2, but their low repeatability questions their suitability; the authors name Stryd the most recommended tool of those analysed.
limitations: 12 male endurance athletes, short submaximal protocols, 2020-era firmware; the criterion is VO2, not mechanical power, so r with VO2 does not establish absolute watts; the abstract does not describe the Garmin or Polar hardware used (do not assume native-watch power). Online 2020, print 2021.
implications: If running power is ingested, treat it as external load whose reliability depends on the device: accept Stryd for load/intensity features and flag Garmin, Polar and RunScribe power as low confidence.
Never mix power from different devices when computing power zones or loads; store the source device with each activity.

verification.notes: Crossref confirms title, Eur J Sport Sci, online 26 Apr 2020 (print Mar 2021), first author Cerezuela-Espejo. Numbers match the Europe PMC abstract. Corrected 'Garmin native' to the abstract's 'Garmin RP'; design changed from experimental-crossover to cross-sectional.
